25	// the rider (home delivery) or the farmer (self-pickup) — who confirms it in
26	// their dashboard. crypto.randomInt avoids Math.random's predictability.
27	function generateHandoverOtp(): string {

29	}
30

32	  id: string
33	  name: string
34	  unit: string | null
35	  stock_qty: number | null
36	  status: string | null
37	  farmer_id: string
38	  price_tier_1_qty: number | null

53	  // mobile, and address below (see the `guest` branch).
54	  const session = getConsumerSessionFromRequest(req)
55	
56	  const body = await req.json().catch(() => null) as

59	        paymentMethod?: string
60	        pickupLocation?: string | null
61	        items?: IncomingItem[]
62	        deliveryType?: string
63	        deliveryAddress?: string | null
64	        deliveryCity?: string | null
65	        deliveryLandmark?: string | null
66	        deliveryPincode?: string | null
67	        deliveryAltPhone?: string | null
68	        idempotencyKey?: string | null

70	      }

143	  const supabase = createClient(

146	  )
147	
148	  // Resolve the authoritative buyer. For accounts we read name/phone from the

151	  let buyerId: string | null = null
152	  let buyerName: string
153	  let buyerPhone: string
154	  let buyerEmail: string | null = null

157	      .from('consumers_auth')
158	      .select('id, name, phone')
159	      .eq('id', session.consumerId)

169	  }

171	  // Idempotency: if this checkout attempt was already saved (double-tap or a
172	  // retry after a lost response), return the existing rows instead of placing
173	  // a second order and decrementing stock again. Guest orders have no
174	  // consumer_id, so we match on the (random UUID) key alone for them.
175	  if (idempotencyKey) {
176	    let existingQuery = supabase
177	      .from('orders')
178	      .select('id, order_code, total_price, delivery_fee')

213	  // Pull live listing rows — never trust prices from the client cart

226	  const listingById = new Map(listings.map((l) => [l.id, l]))

228	  // Harvest-as-product: when a line names a harvest, we sell that harvest's own

input.content:
# Per-harvest delivery choice at checkout

## Context
Trello card "Handling 2 harvests within same checkout": today the cart has **one**
global Pickup-vs-Delivery toggle for the whole checkout. If a buyer has two
harvests with different fulfillment rules (one pickup-only, one delivery-only)
the cart shows a hard "conflict" error and refuses the order. The card wants the
choice made **per harvest** instead:

- Remove the single Pickup/Delivery toggle at the top.
- Put a Pickup / Delivery selector on **each harvest line**; for a harvest that
  doesn't offer home delivery (or is delivery-only), show both buttons but
  **disable** the one that isn't available.
- Move the address / pickup-location entry to **one block at the very end**,
  after the amounts (confirmed layout choice).

**Good news:** `delivery_type` (and the address + `pickup_location` columns) are
already stored **per order row** — each cart line is its own row, and rider
assignment, tracking, and the farmer/consumer order views already read
`delivery_type` per row. So a single farmer order can already hold a mix of
pickup and delivery rows. **No DB/schema change is needed** — the work is the
cart UI and the place-order API payload.

## Files to change

### 1. `src/components/consumer/Cart.tsx` (main work)
Replace the single `deliveryType` state with a per-item map.

- **State:** drop `const [deliveryType, setDeliveryType] = useState(...)`. Add
  `const [deliveryByItem, setDeliveryByItem] = useState<Record<string,'self_pickup'|'home_delivery'>>({})`,
  keyed by `cartKeyOf(item)`.
- **Per-item allowed options** (reuse existing `deliveryModes`/`modeOf`):
  - `canPickup(it)  = modeOf(it) !== 'courier'`
  - `canDeliver(it) = modeOf(it) !== 'pickup'`
  - Every item allows at least one, so the old cart-wide `deliveryConflict`
    branch (lines ~511-524, 1286-1293) is **deleted entirely**.
- **Default selection effect:** for each cart item without a choice yet, default
  to `self_pickup` if `canPickup` else `home_delivery`. Prune stale keys when
  items change.
- **Per-harvest selector UI:** inside each item row in the farmer-group list
  (around lines 1527-1579), add two small buttons `🚶 Pickup` / `🛵 Delivery`.
  Render both always; add `disabled` + greyed style when `!canPickup` /
  `!canDeliver`. Highlight the active one. On click, set `deliveryByItem[key]`.
- **Delete the global "How will you receive your order?" section** (lines
  ~1279-1351).
- **New consolidated "Delivery & pickup details" block at the end** (after the
  farmer groups, before Clear cart — reuse the existing address JSX from lines
  1354-1434 and the per-farmer pickup-location JSX from lines 1624-1700):
  - Show the **address form** if `anyDelivery = items.some(i => deliveryByItem[key]==='home_delivery')`.
  - For each farmer group that has ≥1 pickup item, show its **pickup-location
    picker** (or the village fallback). Move these out of the per-group block.
- **Derived flags** (replace `needsAddress`/`deliveryDetailsMissing`):
  - `anyDelivery` (above) drives the address form + `deliveryDetailsMissing`.
  - `pickupMissing(farmerId)` = group has a pickup item AND farmer has pickup
    locations AND none chosen.
  - `detailsMissing = baseDetailsMissing || (anyDelivery && addressInvalid)`;
    fold `pickupMissing` into each group's `groupDetailsMissing` as today.
- **Per-farmer delivery fee** (lines ~1582, 1521-1523 badge, 1731-1735 button
  amount): `groupHasDelivery = group.some(it => deliveryByItem[cartKeyOf(it)]==='home_delivery')`;
  charge `DELIVERY_FEE_RUPEES` once when `groupHasDelivery`. Badge shows
  "Pickup", "Delivery", or "Pickup + Delivery" (mixed).
- **`placeOrderViaApi`** (lines 539-568): send each item's own type —
  `items: group.map(it => ({ listingId, harvestId, qty, deliveryType: deliveryByItem[cartKeyOf(it)] }))`.
  Send `deliveryAddress`/city/etc. when `anyDelivery`; send
  `pickupLocation: pickupByFarmer[f.farmerId] || null` always (API stamps it on
  pickup rows only). Drop the top-level `deliveryType`.
- **Success-screen `pickupLocation`** (lines 607, 663): use
  `pickupByFarmer[f.farmerId]` when the group has a pickup item.
- **Header subtitle** (lines 1218-1222): make neutral, e.g. "Choose pickup or
  delivery per item".

### 2. `src/app/api/orders/place/route.ts`
Move `delivery_type` from a single request value to per item.

- **`IncomingItem`** (line 17): add `deliveryType?: 'self_pickup' | 'home_delivery'`.
- Per item, resolve `rowDeliveryType` = item's own value (fallback to top-level

Done. Implemented the Trello card **"Handling 2 harvests within same checkout."**

## What changed

**Per-harvest delivery choice** — each cart line now has its own `🚶 Pickup` / `🛵 Delivery` selector. Both buttons always show; the option a produce doesn't offer (from its `delivery_mode`) is disabled/greyed. The single global toggle at the top is gone, and so is the old "these items can't go in one order" conflict error — a cart can now freely mix a pickup-only and a delivery-only harvest.

**Address/pickup moved to the end** — a consolidated "Delivery & pickup details" block sits below all the farmer groups and their amounts, showing the delivery address form only if some item is delivery, plus a pickup-point picker for each farmer that has a pickup item. Payment method and the place-order buttons now follow it (the layout you picked).

**No DB change needed** — `delivery_type`, the address columns, and `pickup_location` were already stored per order row, and rider assignment / order tracking / farmer views already read them per row. So a single farmer's order can hold a mix of pickup and delivery rows.

## Files
- `src/components/consumer/Cart.tsx` — `deliveryByItem` map + `deliveryOf`/`canPickupItem`/`canDeliverItem` helpers + a seed effect; per-item selector UI; consolidated end block.
- `src/app/api/orders/place/route.ts` — accepts per-item `deliveryType`, stamps each row, address only on delivery rows, `pickup_location` only on pickup rows, and the one delivery fee on the first home-delivery row.

## Verification
- `npm run build` compiles clean; `/consumer/cart` renders 200. (The `JSON.parse` lines in the dev log are pre-existing startup noise, not from these changes.)
- I did **not** interactively drive a two-harvest mixed checkout — that needs your seeded Supabase harvests with differing `delivery_mode`. To confirm: add one `pickup`-mode and one `both`/`courier`-mode harvest from the same farmer, check each line's selector (disabled where unavailable), place a COD order, and verify in the `orders` table that the two rows carry different `delivery_type`, address only on the delivery row, `pickup_location` only on the pickup row, and a single `delivery_fee`.

Nothing is committed or pushed yet — let me know if you'd like me to commit (I'll confirm before any push).
